_about: How to re-scrape each estate, so next year's pass is a command and not an
investigation. One entry per estate, written when that estate's pass was
done, with the date it was checked.
`wines` lists the addresses that carry a vintage: `pattern` has {year} in
it and is fed to tools/crawl-pages.py --pattern, `years` is the range the
site actually answers for. `wine` names the wine in BDX_CUVEE_WINES that
the pages belong to, or 'grand' for the grand vin.
`pdfs` says where a technical sheet lives, or that there is none - which
is a finding worth keeping, because 'this estate publishes no fiche' is
the answer to a question that otherwise gets asked every year.
`watch` is what went wrong last time and would go wrong again.

margaux.pdfs: none. No PDF in either sitemap, and /wp-json/wp/v2/media answers 404, so there is no WordPress media library to ask. Margaux publishes no fiche technique: everything is on the vintage pages.

wines.note: 126 vintages, back to 1900. The 1900-1949 half was only fetched on 2026-10-24.
The third wine, made only in those years.

watch: The news feed. /en/actualites/ carries six pages for 2025 alone, and one of them gave the grand vin a season note about Pavillon Blanc's harvest while the vintage page beside it stated the yield, the blend, the season and the tasting note. read-fiches.py now ranks /actualites/ last; if a note looks like it is about the estate rather than the wine, that is where it came from.

One paragraph, two jobs. The vintage pages write the year's story and the wine's tasting as a single block, with inline labels - '... superb length. Blend: 89% cabernet sauvignon ... Climate: Le millesime 2025 est marque ...'. PROSE_STOP now stops at Blend: and Climate:, but the season note still ends on tasting language for 1964 and 2025 and there is no taste field for either.

French on the English page. The 'Climate:' paragraph for 2025 is untranslated on the English URL, so a reader that takes it puts French in an English field - which is what happened to Pavillon Rouge 2025 before the stop was added.
The host. The sitemap says chateau-margaux.com and the manifest holds www.chateau-margaux.com for the pages fetched before 2026-10-24. Comparing the two naively reports every page as missing.

No assemblage before 2005. The pages for 1900-2004 state no blend at all - asked of all 76 with probes looser than the reader's, and none pairs a variety with a percentage. 2005 states only two varieties (85% cabernet sauvignon, 8% merlot) and so has no full blend either.

latour.robots: User-agent: * with /cgi-bin/, /assets/, /uploads/, /application/ disallowed. No Sitemap: line; /sitemap.xml answers with 69 urls.
latour.pdfs: none. No PDF in the sitemap and /wp-json/wp/v2/media answers 404.

wines.note: Every vintage is on this one page behind a #year fragment, so there is no per-vintage address. tools/crawl-pages.py --split is what cuts it into one record per year.

watch: Les Forts de Latour and Le Pauillac de Chateau Latour are DELIBERATELY NOT in BDX_CUVEE_WINES. The site publishes no per-vintage page for either - one descriptive page each, no years in the markup - so there is nothing to file under them. Listing them costs five of the grand vin's own pages, because Latour's extracts never name Chateau Latour in their text and names_another_wine then hands the page to whichever other wine is mentioned: 1966 says Les Forts was first made that year, 1987 says vats were downgraded to generic Pauillac, and 2016/2018/2019 carry the availability line.
1966 is still refused, because chateaux.js records Les Forts as Latour's `second` independently of cuvees.js. One record, one document.

The layout is 'Signature Wine style: <tasting>' then 'Vineyard & harvest Weather conditions: <season>'. Both are registered labels now. If tasting notes start appearing under the season heading again, that is what broke.
Latour does not release a grand vin every year and says so on the page. That is not the same as not making one, so do not mark those vintages not-produced.
No assemblage anywhere. Asked of all 75 documents with no guard and no gate: not one pairs a variety with a percentage.
